rubrics.rubric: Does ABC-Supplier Matrix provide a traceable ABC analysis and characterize every supplier's portfolio?
criterion: ABC classification and revenue share use whs_sales from warehouse_sales_2019_2020.csv and a documented classification method.
For every supplier and ABC class, the matrix reports SKU count, revenue, revenue share, and average inventory turns.
Supplier totals include total SKUs and total revenue share, and the analysis identifies the dominant A-class supplier and the supplier with the most SKUs from the submitted calculations.
The SKU universe, item-code normalization, and any exclusions or joins between transaction and inventory data are documented so reported counts and shares are reproducible.

rubrics.rubric: Does the workbook correctly identify and explain dead stock by supplier?
criterion: Dead stock is identified as positive ON_HAND_QTY with zero warehouse sales in the last six available months, rather than by an unrelated annual proxy alone.
The supplier summary reports dead-stock item count, units on hand, and value at unit cost.
The item-level list contains item code, description, supplier, UNIT_COST, ON_HAND_QTY, and ANNUAL_COGS_2020.
The analysis identifies disproportionate supplier concentrations and notable high-value items and connects them to working capital and warehouse-space use.

rubrics.rubric: Does Demand Volatility & Reorder Analysis correctly analyze every A-class item?
criterion: The sheet contains one row per A-class item from the workbook's ABC classification.
Mean monthly warehouse sales, standard deviation, CV, and the CV greater-than-1.0 volatility flag are calculated using a documented treatment of available and missing months.
Current REORDER_POINT, lead-time-appropriate reorder point, percentage deviation, greater-than-30-percent misalignment flag, and proposed reorder point are reported for each row.
The reorder calculation states its lead-time source and method and uses source-grounded demand and lead-time values.
The analysis states limitations caused by sparse periods, zero demand, or single-observation items without treating a mechanically zero CV as proof of stable demand.

rubrics.rubric: Does Supplier Scorecard apply the required weights to source-grounded supplier metrics?
criterion: Every supplier has on-time delivery rate, order accuracy, average lead time compared with contract terms, quality issue rate, and year-over-year spend trend or a clearly disclosed estimate or limitation.
Component scores use a documented and consistently applied normalization or scoring method.
The composite uses exactly 30% on-time delivery, 25% order accuracy, 20% lead time, 15% quality, and 10% spend trend.
The overall ranking follows from the displayed component scores and composite calculation rather than a hard-coded expected order.

rubrics.rubric: Do the scorecard and contract negotiation brief give complete, data-supported positions for both expiring suppliers?
criterion: Republic National and The Country Vintner or Winebow each receive a clear renewal, conditional-renewal, or non-renewal recommendation.
Each recommendation cites that supplier's on-time delivery, average lead time, total spend and share, SKU count, dead-stock contribution, and contract end date.

Negotiation targets are numeric and tied to displayed supplier metrics, contract terms, task-provided performance targets, or cited benchmarks with a quantitative rationale; assumptions used because the data cannot determine a target are justified and sensitivity-tested.
If non-renewal or partial exit is recommended, the brief estimates the SKU migration scope and addresses transition risk.

rubrics.rubric: Does the revised SOP replace static reorder points with an operational demand-and-lead-time method?
criterion: The SOP removes or redlines the annual static reorder-point method and supplies a reproducible demand, lead-time, and safety-stock formula.
The SOP states which source supplies lead time for each supplier and why that source is appropriate.
Seasonal demand or promotions are incorporated through a documented adjustment process.
The procedure defines who recalculates the values, how often they are refreshed, and how exceptions are handled.

rubrics.rubric: Does the SOP revision preserve the original procedure as a reviewable redline and implement the required controls?
criterion: The original six top-level sections and all nine process steps remain visible and in their original order.
Changes are shown with tracked revisions, strikethrough and additions, or explicit redline markers that distinguish retained, deleted, and added text.
The revision introduces tiered replenishment frequencies driven by ABC classification and references the documented inefficiencies by stable numbers.
The revision includes inventory turns of at least 9x, fill rate of at least 97%, and dead stock of at most 1.5%, together with monitoring cadence and escalation triggers.

rubrics.rubric: Is the three-sheet workbook structurally complete and visibly integrated?
criterion: The workbook contains exactly three worksheets in the requested order; an Excel-safe abbreviation of the overlength second worksheet name is acceptable when the full requested title appears in-sheet.
The reorder analysis is driven by the ABC-Supplier Matrix A-class list.
Supplier Scorecard references dead stock from the first sheet and reorder misalignment counts from the second sheet.
Inventory-turn results from the first sheet are connected to the workbook's overall inventory-performance discussion.
